Q101.q: We plan to choose a package without accommodation, and our priests are coming with us. On days when no Mass is planned at WYD, how can we arrange a nearby parish where our priest can celebrate Mass for our group?
Q101.a: Groups using packages with accommodation will be allocated to most parishes in Seoul, and the allocated groups will have priority in using those parishes. Please understand that you will need to request use during times when the allocated groups are not using them.

Q102.q: Will safety and awareness materials on heretical groups, cults and similar activities be provided for pilgrims preparing for WYD?
Q102.a: The Committee on Pseudo-Religions of the Catholic Bishops' Conference of Korea is currently preparing guidance materials, and the draft is under review. After the review, it will be translated into the official languages and distributed.

Q103.q:
It seems we should state the date of entry not as the date of arrival in Seoul but as the date relevant to the entry visa for the Days in the Dioceses.
Can participants in the Days in the Dioceses apply for a visa using the address of the Seoul Organising Committee?
Q103.a: The date of entry into Korea must be stated as the actual date of arrival in Korea on your flight, regardless of whether you take part in the Days in the Dioceses. Also, since visas are applied for on the basis of documents issued by WYD, we recommend entering the Local Organising Committee's information as your address and contact details in Korea when applying. However, the dates of entry and departure must match your actual flight schedule.

Q104.q: Will allergy information be shared with those in charge of the Days in the Dioceses? Registration and payment of the fee and contribution for the Days in the Dioceses will presumably be done separately, but will a link be provided? Do we have to enter everything again completely separately?
Q104.a: In applying for the Days in the Dioceses, only the number of participants has been registered so far; detailed information will be requested later when the list is submitted to the diocese. Allergies and other special requirements will be collected at that time. The donation for the Days in the Dioceses will be paid to the participating diocese, by bank transfer.

Q105.q: Can the diocese hosting the Days in the Dioceses support the cost of transport to Seoul?
Q105.a: The Days in the Dioceses are run differently in each diocese. For travel to the main event after the Days in the Dioceses, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q106.q: When taking part in the Days in the Dioceses, is transport from the airport to the host diocese, from Seoul to the host diocese, and from the host diocese to accommodation in Seoul after the Days in the Dioceses provided by the organisers or included in the package, or must each delegation or group arrange it themselves?
Q106.a: The Days in the Dioceses are run differently in each diocese. For transport from the airport to the host diocese and from the host diocese to the main event, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q107.q: When does registration for the Days in the Dioceses start?
Q107.a: Registration for the Days in the Dioceses has already started. You can apply in person, by phone, by email or through the Days in the Dioceses website (https://wyd2027did.org). However, it is difficult to apply to dioceses whose prepared capacity for the Days in the Dioceses has already been filled.

Q108.q: Is the period of the Days in the Dioceses also covered by insurance?
Q108.a: The dioceses running the Days in the Dioceses are arranging event insurance. However, pilgrims should arrange their own personal travel insurance.

Q109.q: Is there an accommodation solution for those arriving for the Days in the Dioceses before 29 July 2027?
Q109.a: The Days in the Dioceses are run differently in each diocese. For accommodation in the case of early arrival, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q110.q: Will minors stay in homestays when taking part in the Days in the Dioceses?
Q110.a: Currently, most dioceses are preparing homestays as the standard option. When minors take part in the Days in the Dioceses, they will stay in homestays only when accompanied by a guardian. Please make sure you have enough guardians for the number of minors. For accommodation other than homestays, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q111.q: It seems many dioceses are already full. In that case, is it too late for us to find a diocese?
Q111.a: As of 7 October, 55% of the capacity prepared for pilgrims taking part in the Days in the Dioceses has been taken. There is still room, and even if applications exceed the capacity prepared by the Church in Korea for the Days in the Dioceses, there is flexibility to accommodate them. All pilgrims who wish to take part in the Days in the Dioceses are welcome. Please do not worry, and apply.

Q112.q: From when is registration for the Days in the Dioceses valid? Some dioceses have already contacted us, but actual WYD registration does not start until October. Is registration for the Days in the Dioceses alone already valid, or does it only become valid after registering for WYD?
Q112.a:
Registration for the Days in the Dioceses is carried out separately from the main event. Registration for the Days in the Dioceses has already started and proceeds in the following three steps.
1) Registration of the number of participants 2) Registration of the list of participants 3) Payment of the pilgrim donation
For reference, once the capacity prepared by the diocese you wish to attend has been filled, you can no longer apply to that diocese.

Q113.q: Also, is the date of travel from the Days in the Dioceses to WYD 2 August or 3 August?
Q113.a: The Days in the Dioceses take place over five days and four nights, from 29 July to 2 August 2027. After the programme on 2 August, participants travel to the main event on the same day.

Q114.q: How are international movements, communities and lay associations being integrated into the DID programme while expressing their own distinctive charisms?
Q114.a: The Days in the Dioceses are oriented towards pilgrims' experience of the local Church. For the integration of your own charism with the Days in the Dioceses programme, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q115.q: What is the cost, and how is payment made? Is it free, or is there a separate fee? Is payment made at the time of registration, or directly to the diocese?
Q115.a: The pilgrim donation for the Days in the Dioceses is the same in all dioceses: $100. Most dioceses provide a homestay, breakfast, event insurance and souvenirs. For meals other than breakfast, transport and other costs, please contact the diocese you wish to attend directly.

Q116.q: We are very concerned about the situation regarding the World Cup Stadium and the Peace Park. The stadium holds 60,000 people, so there will be no opportunity to rotate people fairly. It will feel very unfair to many, and this plan will still result in many young people being excluded and turned away. For each of the three events held at the Peace Park/World Cup Stadium, on what basis will groups be selected for indoor and outdoor seats? Is it by lottery? What can be done so that this does not look exclusionary? It looks like a situation that divides the 'haves' and the 'have-nots'. Young people need something that is not exclusive. We hope the Church will not once again become an organisation that rejects them.
Q116.a: As those responsible for the event, we fully understand the questioner's concern. We will set principles and criteria for communication and allocation so that such worries do not turn into unfairness. We will also put in place various considerations and means of communication so that sitting inside the stadium does not become a privilege and sitting in the Peace Park does not mean being left out.

Q117.q: Central America and the Caribbean do not appear in the divisions for the Way of the Cross. Will they be considered?
Q117.a: The continental divisions for the Way of the Cross and all events of the main event are based on the continents as divided by the Holy See.

Q118.q: For the main events such as the Opening Mass, the Papal Welcome Ceremony and the Way of the Cross, on what basis will areas inside and outside the stadium be allocated to groups and pilgrims? We would like to know whether delegations from Bishops' Conferences, for example, will have priority, and whether allocation will be by advance assignment or by lottery. Also, what measures will be in place so that pilgrims exceeding the stadium's capacity can still take part meaningfully in the events and Masses on site?
Q118.a: Seats in the stadium will be allocated in advance, but priority will not be given to certain clergy. The Youth Day should give priority consideration to marginalised young people, people with disabilities and youth representatives from each country. Various arrangements and considerations for pilgrims in the park are being discussed. We are preparing various considerations and means of communication so that the stadium does not become a privilege and so that sitting in the park does not feel like missing out.

Q119.q: We are worried that the events will be held behind closed doors inside the stadium and feel isolated. Even if the Holy Father wishes to be a shepherd who draws close, it may be hard to feel that this is an event for everyone.
Q119.a: We are considering various ways to ensure that the event is not held in isolation within the stadium. We are preparing various ways to connect not only with young people beyond the stadium and Seoul, on the other side of the world, but also with young people outside the stadium.

Q120.q: Is there currently clear information on where the transport will drop us off and roughly how far young people will have to walk from there to the closing Mass venue?
Q120.a: The operating plan is currently being drawn up, and a transport/travel guide for pilgrims will be distributed shortly before the event.

Q121.q: Please answer regarding the confidential information on the closing Mass venue. Do you mean that it cannot be shared with the bishops and leaders who will ask us about it? Is it all right to share it internally? Or do you mean that this information must stay within this room?
Q121.a: Information about the closing Mass venue may be shared internally at the level of Bishops' Conferences and dioceses. However, it must not be shared through public media (broadcasting, the internet, YouTube, newspaper articles, personal social media, etc.) before the official announcement. Please wait prayerfully until it is announced.

Q122.q: We would like to ask about the closing Mass venue. Could priests be placed in areas A1 and A3? That way, young people could also take places in area A2, right in front of the stage.
Q122.a: The areas in front of the stage will be specially managed. Seating for priests is planned in a separate front area, and youth representatives, young people from marginalised backgrounds and special participants will be managed separately and seated at the front of the stage. The specific seating arrangements will be confirmed only after pilgrim registration closes.

Q123.q: Will a list of items that can and cannot be brought to the Opening Mass and the closing Mass be published in advance? For example, can we pitch a tent at the closing Mass?
Q123.a: Permitted items will be announced in advance and, as a matter of common sense, will be limited to what is needed for one night of sleeping outdoors. Pitching tents is not allowed.

Q124.q: For the final day's events at Seoul Air Base, will volunteers be deployed to guide pilgrims to their designated areas? At the last event, some pilgrims tended not to follow their designated areas and tried to take places near the stage.
Q124.a: The LOC is preparing all events expected to draw large crowds with safety as the top priority. For the safety of pilgrims, we will prepare and carry out many measures, including the deployment of volunteers.

Q125.q: How can we get to Seoul Air Base to attend the Vigil and the Mass? Can we get there by public transport?
Q125.a:
You will travel by subway and on foot. Details will be provided in a
transport/travel guide for pilgrims to be distributed shortly before the event.

Q126.q: Is there a contingency plan in case of heavy rain during the Vigil?
Q126.a:
In case of heavy rain during the Vigil, we plan to use large tents, hangars and other facilities set up on site,
and we are preparing specific measures for wet weather.

Q127.q: What measures will be taken to protect pilgrims at outdoor events such as the Vigil and the closing Mass against the heatwaves and heavy rain expected during WYD? Will the LOC provide shade, drinking water and rest areas, and can you tell us what participants should prepare themselves, such as hats and parasols?
Q127.a: We plan to set up waiting areas and tents within the venue to cope with heatwaves and heavy rain, but since it will be difficult to accommodate everyone, each person should bring their own hat and parasol. We will remind you of this again when registration opens.

Q128.q: If more pilgrims than expected gather at the Vigil venue so that capacity is exceeded or congestion occurs, what entry management and alternative participation measures will be in place so that no pilgrim is unable to enter? In Lisbon, some pilgrims could not get into the Vigil venue because of congestion.
Q128.a: We are preparing to provide guidance for staggered movement by group so that as many pilgrims as possible can come to the closing Mass.

Q129.q: How will concelebration by priests and liturgical participation by deacons be organised at the main Masses? Please let us know whether separate advance registration or verification of eligibility is required, and whether vestments such as the alb and stole must be prepared individually.
Q129.a: For the Opening Mass, we are considering the seats behind the stage as dedicated seating for priests. For the closing Mass, in order to bring young people closer to the altar, we are considering placing the priests' seating at the far left and right ends of the young people's area. Commemorative albs and stoles will be distributed free of charge on site on the day.

Q130.q: What opportunities and procedures are there at WYD for international youth organisations and external organisers to propose, take part in and collaborate on general events, workshops or side events? What must organisations wishing to take part in the Youth Festival prepare, and what are the procedures for applying for and allocating spaces and booths, and the participation costs?
Q130.a: Organisations wishing to take part in the Youth Festival can apply for the project they want to run through the registration system. Projects in various genres are possible, such as performances, talks, exhibitions, prayer and praise, and workshops, and participation is free of charge. All countries can take part. The final selection of participating teams is made by the Holy See and the LOC, and venues are allocated and provided by the LOC.

Q131.q: How do young people from other countries perform at their Youth Festival? Is registration required? Are venues allocated? Do they have to pay a participation fee?
Q131.a: The Youth Festival and the Vocations Fair run only during the main event, in the diocese hosting the main event. Groups or organisations wishing to take part can apply through the registration system. There is no participation fee for the Youth Festival; for the Vocations Fair, a booth fee of 700 US dollars for one booth or 1,300 US dollars for two booths is required. For the Youth Festival, the team running the project can choose the language as it wishes. Most include English.

Q132.q: On which website can we find the procedure for taking part in the Youth Festival and the Vocations Fair? How can we find out? To make this experience even richer, can we publicise this information widely in our countries? We would like to know when, where and in what form the City of Joy, the Vocations Fair and the Youth Festival will run at WYD, whether they will be spread across several dioceses, and whether there will be programmes for different language groups.
Q132.a: You can apply for the Youth Festival and the Vocations Fair through the registration system. The registration system is scheduled to open around the end of October and can be accessed through the official website (https://wydseoul.org/). To make this experience even richer, we ask you to promote the official website widely.

Q133.q: How do priests register to hear confessions during the 'Park of Reconciliation'?
Q133.a: Priests register in the registration system together with their pilgrim group. Since pilgrim group registration is done by the group leader, priests who wish to hear confessions at the 'Park of Reconciliation' should tell their group leader the dates and times they are available. Priests travelling alone without a group can register as a one-person group.

Q134.q: What does a 'booth' at the Vocations Fair mean?
Q134.a: At the Vocations Fair (Catholic Cultural Fair), a 'booth' means a 3m x 3m space made up of a tent or stand given to each religious institute or apostolic/devotional association taking part in the fair. Each religious institute can apply for up to two.

Q135.q: What does the Vocations Fair consist of? What exactly is the participation fee used for?
Q135.a: The Vocations Fair is an event that helps pilgrims discern their own calling by sharing with them the charism and spirituality of each participating religious institute or association. The participation fee is used to rent the venue and set up the booths.

Q136.q: What are the criteria for selecting priests to hear confessions? Can only selected priests take part, or can anyone? Do priests need to indicate their participation when registering?
Q136.a: Any priest can take part, but they must be registered in the registration system for identity verification.

Q137.q: How many days will the Park of Reconciliation operate during this event? For how many hours a day will confession be available? Can young people move freely in and out of the park? During the Jubilee event in Rome, access to the places where confessions were heard was very limited, almost controlled.
Q137.a:
The 'Park of Reconciliation' will run from Tuesday to Friday of the main event week, from 1 pm to 5 pm.
Because of the seal of confession, young people cannot walk freely around the park.
Entry to the park is possible along a set route under the guidance of volunteers. Anyone who is prepared can receive the sacrament of confession.

Q138.q: If we stay in a hotel, how will we be guided on the way to the catechesis location?
Q138.a: Groups that have arranged their own accommodation, such as hotels, should also travel based on their allocated catechesis location. Information on catechesis locations and how to get there will be announced later.

Q139.q: In Panama, catechesis materials were provided before the pre-events and the main event. Will that be the case this time too?
Q139.a: We expect them to be provided before the main event if possible.

Q140.q: Even if our accommodation is some distance from Seoul, can we be allocated to the nearest catechesis location, taking the location of our accommodation into account?
Q140.a: The route and travel time from your accommodation to the catechesis location vary depending on where your accommodation is, so please check using a map app or similar, based on the address of the location you are given.

Q141.q: How do we apply for catechesis, and will it be run as an interactive, dynamic programme as in Lisbon?
Q141.a: Catechesis will be organised by estimating the number of participants after the speakers have been selected. We expect it to be run similarly to Lisbon.

Q142.q: Can you tell us which languages will be used during catechesis?
Q142.a: We expect it to be held in the six official languages.

Q143.q: When will catechesis locations be confirmed and announced?
Q143.a: They will be confirmed in stages from about one month before the event and announced by email.

Q144.q: If the total number of registered participants exceeds the capacity of the catechesis locations, how will venues and capacity be secured and allocated so that all pilgrims can take part in catechesis?
Q144.a: Catechesis locations are continually being checked, and we will do our best to ensure that all participants who have applied for catechesis can attend.

Q145.q: Do we need to give advance notice if we want to plan a catechesis session?
Q145.a: The speakers and themes for catechesis are selected by the DLFL.

Q146.q: What should we do to take part as a catechesis facilitator?
Q146.a: We will provide information as we proceed with discussions with the DLFL regarding catechesis.
